paper.title_en: Complementary mechanisms of critical quantum metrology
paper.abstract_en: Critical metrology conventionally exploits enhanced susceptibility to a system parameter near a phase transition. Here we identify a complementary mechanism for critically enhanced estimation of intrinsic system parameters via suppressed quantum noise rather than enhanced response. We demonstrate both mechanisms in coherently radiating spin states (CRSS)-correlated states of $N$ spin-$1/2$ particles defined as asymptotic eigenstates of the collective-spin lowering operator with complex eigenvalue $r e^{-iφ}$. At the critical value $r=1$, CRSS exhibit a second-order transition. We show that near criticality, estimation of $r$ benefits from enhanced susceptibility despite increased noise, whereas estimation of $φ$ benefits from suppressed quantum noise without enhanced response. Remarkably, both yield the same estimation error $\sim N^{-2/3}$, improving over the standard quantum limit $N^{-1/2}$. For $φ$, this establishes quantum-enhanced metrology of phases intrinsic to the critical system, rather than phases externally encoded by interferometry. We demonstrate these results for CRSS realizations in both dissipative (superradiant) and Hamiltonian (Ising) systems relevant to cavity QED and trapped ions, where fast preparation of CRSS is shown possible thanks to gap opening. Applications to metrology of coupling rates and phases or optical lengths are discussed.
